clue.text: Nietzsche's agreed on duplication of his core notes

parts.note: a German philosopher saying yes would say ja

indicators.note: duplication means the letter is written down twice over

parts.note: his refers to Nietzsche, and the central letter of that nine-letter name is Z

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader wonders whether the German philosopher endorsed repeating his central notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to Nietzsche: his core is the fifth of nine letters, Z, and 'duplication of' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The music genre is made of notes played, so 'notes' stands loosely for a style of music.

clue.text: One who's innocent getting lawyer's letter

parts.note: a lamb is the stock emblem of innocence
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: An innocent party is handed a letter from a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Film about Saint Alban transformed the state of Hollywood

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: Hollywood is in California, abbreviated CA

explanation.surface: A film about the English martyr Saint Alban changed the whole mood of Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 1942 Bogart and Bergman wartime picture, an example of a film.

clue.text: Old leader of 19 Down missing as 11 haven demolished

indicators.note: demolished says the remaining letters are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order
missing says the named letters are dropped from the combined letters

parts.note: the answer to 11 Across, the striped animal
read as A's, two letter As

explanation.surface: Reads like a cross-reference puzzle about a ruined sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: ZEBRA plus HAVEN, losing both As ('missing as' = without A's), leaves ZEBRHVEN, which 'demolished' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid Brezhnev led the Soviet Union from 1964 to 1982, so he was an old leader of the Russian people.

clue.text: Ducks munch on cookie

indicators.note: munch pictures the two letters closing round another like a mouth

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, so two ducks are two Os
RE means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Some ducks peck away at a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous American sandwich biscuit, so it is a kind of cookie.

clue.text: Admit five equals four to stop causing an argument

indicators.note: Admit means let in, so the stopping word takes the sum inside it

parts.note: to die is to stop, as an engine dies
V is the Roman numeral five
is is a way of saying equals
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: Conceding that five equals four would stop a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' means let in: the Roman-numeral sum is let into the stopping word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divisive splits people into opposing camps, provoking disagreement.

clue.text: In bed, love the ultimate in baldness?

indicators.note: In says the zero letter goes within the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bald man in bed with his partner muses on hair loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'as bald as a coot', from the bird's white forehead patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially nothing is balder than this waterbird, so it is the extreme of hairlessness.

clue.text: Fat Controller after salad with crusts lost a stone

indicators.note: after puts the fat word behind the trimmed salad
the crusts are the outer letters, so the salad loses its first and last

parts.note: a baster is a tool that controls the fat spooned over a roast

explanation.surface: Thomas the Tank Engine's Fat Controller ate a crustless salad and lost a stone in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Controller is the railway boss in the British children's books Thomas the Tank Engine; here he is a baster.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft white mineral used for carving, it is a type of stone.

clue.text: Tiny boy performing lead role in Shakespeare

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A small boy takes the lead in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Timon of Athens is the leading part in that play.

clue.text: Greek head of reconstruction invests in informal currency

indicators.note: invests means clothes or surrounds, so the Greek letter wraps round the next word

parts.note: the word reconstruction starts with R, which in Greek is the letter rho
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek official leading a recovery puts money into slang cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek is not a person: it is the Greek name for R, the head of 'reconstruction'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is old British slang for money, so an informal word for cash.

clue.text: Hide barcode pattern uniquely identifying this?

definitions.text: Hide barcode pattern uniquely identifying this?

parts.words: Hide barcode pattern uniquely identifying this?
parts.note: an animal whose striped hide looks like a barcode, and whose stripes are unique to each individual

explanation.surface: Suggests concealing the stripes on a product label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb meaning conceal, but it is a noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Each striped African equine has a stripe pattern as individual as a fingerprint, like a barcode.

clue.text: Soprano can finally paint picture

parts.note: a mezzo is a mezzo-soprano, a type of soprano voice
a tin is a can

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word paint

explanation.surface: A singer is at last able to paint a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a print made by an engraving method that gives soft tones, so a kind of picture.

clue.text: Charlie Chan interrupts private investigator in Latin? It's all backwards

indicators.note: interrupts names a piece going inside another; here the roles are switched, so Chan is the one split open

parts.note: taken as written: Charlie Chan, the fictional detective

indicators.note: in names one piece put within another; the roles are switched, so the investigator holds the Latin letter

explanation.surface: The detective Charlie Chan breaks in on a Latin-speaking private eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all backwards' warns that both 'interrupts' and 'in' work the wrong way round: the detective's name is split open, and the investigator holds the Latin letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is the silent-film comedian, so his forename stands for his surname.

clue.text: Caught Nazi battling to overthrow king

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi

explanation.surface: A captured Nazi was fighting to topple a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In this board game the aim is checkmate, defeating the opposing king.

clue.text: Beginners try spelling bees and win in an unusual way

indicators.note: in an unusual way says the letters are set out differently

explanation.surface: Novices enter spelling bees and win with odd tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers to any activity, informally, are those just starting out.

clue.text: Short men sensibly don't party on these evenings

definitions.text: sensibly don't party on these evenings

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
chess pieces are called men, and knights are among them

explanation.surface: Advice that short people should stay in on certain nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday to Thursday evenings, before a working day, are when sensible people avoid late parties.

clue.text: Attended to observe material

definitions.meaning: ..., as on a class or meeting, watching without taking part

explanation.surface: Someone came along to inspect some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a glossy woven fabric, and split in two it means watched a meeting from a seat.

clue.text: Silly Englishman losing half his marbles?

definitions.text: Silly Englishman losing half his marbles?

indicators.note: silly says the kept letters are jumbled
losing half keeps just the first half of the ten-letter word

explanation.surface: A daft Englishman is going a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five letters ENGLI are rearranged. 'Losing his marbles' means going mad, but the Earl behind the name lost (removed) the Parthenon marbles from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl who took the Parthenon sculptures to Britain gave his title to the marbles.

clue.text: Worry about prostate, perhaps; it's a dangerous world

indicators.note: about says the worrying word turns round

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester
the prostate is an example of a gland

explanation.surface: A man frets about his prostate in a risky world.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal underworld of organised mobs is a dangerous sphere.

clue.text: Gun for man in service at the front

definitions.meaning: to gun an engine is to speed it up

definitions.text: man in service at the front
definitions.meaning: a clergyman, who leads a church service from the front

explanation.surface: A weapon for a soldier on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' and 'service at the front' suggest war; it is an engine and a church.
explanation.definitionFit: It means race an engine, and is short for Reverend, a cleric leading worship.

clue.text: Devious Iran's detaining America's countrymen

indicators.note: detaining says the rearranged letters hold the American piece
devious means winding, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: US for America, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Crafty Iran is holding American citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with 4 Down, the people of one nation are fellow countrymen.

clue.text: On reflection, it never keeps happening

indicators.note: On reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
keeps means holds within, so the words it never hold the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, something that never happens keeps on happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'keeps happening' as the definition, but 'keeps' is the indicator that the words hold the letters; the definition is just 'happening'.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or incident is a synonym of a happening.

clue.text: When we might regularly hear 19 Across speak of issue with confusion

definitions.text: When we might regularly hear 19 Across

indicators.note: speak of says the words are said aloud, sounding like the answer

parts.note: issue means offspring, a son; confusion is a daze

explanation.surface: A churchgoer hears the vicar preach on a muddled matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 Across is REV, a clergyman, who preaches weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Church services are held on the weekly Christian day of rest, so that is when the vicar is heard.

clue.text: Get down half of Guinness — it's black and white and cold

parts.note: to get something down is to write it, to pen it

indicators.note: half of keeps the first four of the eight letters

explanation.surface: Down half a pint of Guinness, the stout famous for being black and white and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the stout the black-and-white thing; it is the Antarctic bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless Antarctic bird has black and white plumage and lives in freezing places.

clue.text: Two characters boxed in spar, one with two black eyes

parts.note: the two letters held inside the word spar are ...

explanation.surface: A boxer sparring ends up with two black eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'P and A' as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The bamboo-eating bear has black patches round its eyes, like a bruised boxer.

clue.text: Great place, upstanding top-class president? Not quite

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means reading upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as AI

indicators.note: not quite drops the final letter

parts.note: POTUS is short for President of the United States

explanation.surface: A tribute to an upright, first-rate president that falls a bit short.
explanation.definitionFit: An imagined ideal society is the perfect place.

clue.text: Quaking at animal after daughter spotted creature in the house

indicators.note: after puts the shaken letters behind the daughter letter
quaking means shaking, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A girl trembles at the sight of an animal in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted breed is a dog, a creature kept as a household pet.

clue.text: Mould covering cold chop

indicators.note: covering says the mould goes round the cold letter

parts.note: a die is a mould for shaping metal
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Mould has grown over a cold pork chop.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into small cubes is a synonym of to chop finely.

clue.text: Orca shot with a bow

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A killer whale is shot by an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical instruction tells string players to resume using the bow after plucking.

clue.text: Mature reaction to terrible joke on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a groan is the usual response to a bad pun

explanation.surface: A grown-up response to a bad joke broadcast on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully developed, adult, is a synonym of mature.

clue.text: Almost the end of the day; time flies

indicators.note: flies means leaves, so the time letter departs

parts.note: night falls at the close of the day

explanation.surface: It is nearly nightfall; time flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time flies' looks like the proverb but means T leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: It means near, nearly, as in 'well-nigh impossible'.

clue.text: One doubting value of pricy nick-nacks

indicators.note: value of says the letters are taken from the words, nested in them

explanation.surface: Someone questions what expensive trinkets are worth.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Oscar Wilde: such a person knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic distrusts others' motives, so is one doubting.

clue.text: Shave end of pin connecting appliance to ground

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word pin

parts.note: earthing is wiring an appliance to the ground for safety

explanation.surface: Describes wiring a plug's pin to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is a narrow escape, so the word alone can mean one.
